Formulation
Predisposing: History of intermittent anxiety/panic symptoms.  
Precipitating: Acute insect sting leading to fear of severe allergic reaction.  
Perpetuating: Limited immediate social support; lack of prior coping strategies for health-related anxiety.  
Protective: Engaged with healthcare promptly; displays reasonable insight and willingness to follow medical advice.

Mental Health Care Plan Details

Principal Problem:
- Patient Goal(s):
  • Feel reassured and in control when experiencing health concerns  
  • Reduce current anxiety about possible allergic reaction
- Clinical Goal(s):
  • Provide clear information on signs of anaphylaxis and appropriate actions  
  • Teach immediate coping strategies for acute anxiety
- Actions (Patient):
  • Read provided information link on anaphylaxis  
  • Obtain and take over-the-counter antihistamine as instructed  
  • Monitor for warning signs (lip/tongue swelling, breathing difficulty) and seek urgent care if they occur  
  • Practice slow, diaphragmatic breathing when feeling anxious
- Actions (Clinician/GP):
  • Supplied education on anaphylaxis signs and management  
  • Advised antihistamine use; clarified dosing options  
  • Encouraged prompt re-contact or emergency attendance if symptoms worsen  
  • Offered follow-up consult if anxiety persists or escalates

Secondary Problem: Not applicable (no additional mental health issue identified)

Patient Education, Emergency Care & Relapse Prevention
- Education Given: Yes. Topics Covered: recognition of anaphylaxis, use of antihistamines, when to attend ED, reassurance techniques
- Early Warning Signs of Relapse/Worsening: Lip/tongue swelling, breathing difficulty, stridor, spreading rash
- Coping Strategies: Slow breathing, early medical contact, reviewing provided educational material
